chapterName: Middle Republic: The Fall of Carthage and Corinth (167-133 BCE)

questions.question: What did Hasdrubal's wife do when her husband surrendered to Scipio?
options: She fled the city by sea
She was taken to Rome as a hostage
She begged Scipio to spare him
She cursed him and walked into the burning temple
questions.explanation: Watching from a rampart, she blessed Scipio, cursed her husband for cowardice, and walked into the burning temple with their children. Hasdrubal had surrendered in exchange for his life and freedom.
questions.sourceQuote: His wife, watching from a rampart, blessed Scipio, cursed her husband for his cowardice, and walked into the burning temple with their children.

questions.question: After Carthage agreed to disarm in 149 BC, what happened to its warships?
options: They were sailed to Rome as trophies
They were sold to Greek merchants
They were burned in the harbour at Utica
They were sunk at the harbour mouth
They were handed to the Numidians
questions.explanation: Carthage's warships sailed to Utica and were burned in the harbour. Only afterwards did Rome reveal its real demand that the city be abandoned.
questions.sourceQuote: Carthage's warships sailed to Utica and were burned in the harbour.

questions.question: What did Hasdrubal do inside Carthage in 148 BC?
options: Overthrew the civilian leaders and took command
Was executed by the city council
questions.explanation: Hasdrubal overthrew Carthage's civilian leaders and took command himself. That same year a new Roman commander failed to take several towns loyal to Carthage.
questions.sourceQuote: Inside the city, Hasdrubal overthrew the civilian leaders and took command himself.

questions.question: What symbolic act involving Rome and Carthage took place in 1985?
options: The mayors of Rome and Carthage signed a peace treaty
Rome lifted the ancient curse on the site
questions.explanation: In 1985 the mayors of Rome and modern Carthage signed a symbolic peace treaty. After 146 BC, Rome had laid a curse on anyone who tried to resettle the site.
questions.sourceQuote: In 1985 the mayors of Rome and modern Carthage signed a symbolic peace treaty.

questions.question: How did the Senate respond to the peace deals that beaten Roman generals made with Numantia?
options: It exiled both generals to Greece
It ratified them after long debate
It accepted one and rejected the other
It doubled the tribute Numantia owed
It refused them and handed a general to the Numantines
questions.explanation: The Senate refused to honour either deal and handed the beaten general over to the Numantines as a prisoner. One treaty had been negotiated by a young officer whose family the Numantines trusted.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate refused to honour either deal, and simply handed the beaten general over to the Numantines as a prisoner.

questions.question: Who held out to the end in the Temple of Eshmoun and burned it down around themselves?
questions.explanation: About 900 Roman deserters who had fought for Carthage knew they could expect no mercy. They held out in the temple of Eshmoun, a Carthaginian god of healing, and set it alight.
questions.sourceQuote: About 900 Roman deserters who had fought for Carthage knew they could expect no mercy.

questions.question: How long did Carthage's Punic language continue to be spoken in North Africa?
options: It died out within a generation
questions.explanation: Punic was still spoken in North Africa until the 7th century AD. Local towns in the province of Africa also kept much of their own government and culture.
questions.sourceQuote: Local towns kept much of their own government and culture, and the Punic language of Carthage was still spoken in North Africa until the 7th century AD.

questions.question: Which Achaean League ambition did Rome keep blocking, souring relations before the war of 146 BC?
questions.explanation: Rome blocked the League's wish to absorb Sparta, and had also taken thousands of Achaean hostages. In 148 BC the League conquered Sparta anyway.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome had taken thousands of Achaean hostages during its war with Macedonia, and it kept blocking the League's ambitions, above all its wish to absorb Sparta.

questions.question: After Scipio's night attack broke into Carthage, how did Hasdrubal make surrender unthinkable?
options: He sent Scipio a declaration of no quarter
He burned the city's grain stores
He tortured Roman prisoners to death on the walls
He sank ships in the harbour mouth
questions.explanation: Hasdrubal tortured Roman prisoners to death on the walls in full view of their comrades. Carthaginian councillors who protested were executed too.
questions.sourceQuote: Hasdrubal, the general now ruling Carthage, answered by torturing Roman prisoners to death on the walls in full view of their comrades.

questions.question: Who led the large Roman army that landed at Utica in 149 BC?
questions.explanation: The army was led by both consuls, the two chief magistrates Rome elected each year. One ancient account puts it at 84,000 men; modern historians estimate 40,000 to 50,000.
questions.sourceQuote: It was led by both of that year's consuls, the two chief magistrates Rome elected annually to command its armies.
